metric_note: Task-macro pass rate: each task scores passes/trials, the arm scores the mean. This follows the SkillsBench/Terminal-Bench shape but is NOT comparable to SkillsBench numbers: they average 5 trials to our 3, they award no partial credit, and they inject skills as system context while we require the agent to discover them, so our arms measure discovery and use together. SkillsBench reports +16.2pp average from curated skills (range +4.5 to +51.9, with 16 of 84 tasks negative); this corpus reported +72.2pp with zero regressions, which is an instrument fault, not a finding. Retired as evidence about any setup. See references/DECISION_PLAN.md.

setup_lift.label: Setup change, same model
setup_lift.power_note: 19 tasks changed direction, enough for a two-sided test to reach significance.

model_lift.label: Model upgrade, same setup
model_lift.power_note: Only 1 task changed direction. Even if every one of them had moved the same way, the smallest two-sided p this sample can produce is 1.0. Read this as a direction, not as proof.

setup_on_strong.label: Setup change on the stronger model
setup_on_strong.power_note: 21 tasks changed direction, enough for a two-sided test to reach significance.

stacked.label: Both changes together
stacked.power_note: 22 tasks changed direction, enough for a two-sided test to reach significance.

skill_vs_model.label: Stronger model alone vs base model with the skill
skill_vs_model.power_note: 18 tasks changed direction, enough for a two-sided test to reach significance.

caveats: RETIRED as product evidence 2026-09-19. All 25 skills tested here are synthetic and exist on no user's machine; 55% of checks test a house convention the prompt withholds, so the no-skill arm could not pass them by construction. Kept as a harness and mechanism test only.
Every task is drawn from one person's real session logs. n equals one machine, so this measures this setup, not setups in general.
Prompts are identical across arms and never mention that a skill exists, so the with-skill arms measure discovery and use together, not use alone.
The verifier is a fixed script that runs against the finished workspace and never sees which arm produced it.

Each task asserts a house convention that is arbitrary by construction, roughly fourteen checks deep, and nowhere in the prompt. An agent without the skill has no way to guess it, so the no-skill arms sit near zero and the gap measures convention compliance rather than general task ability.
